checks.s: The redline changes the withdrawal notice period from 30 calendar days to no more than 15 calendar days.
The redline modifies or deletes the requirement that a withdrawing party return or destroy shared materials within 15 business days of the withdrawal effective date.
The redline adds an exception providing that materials already reviewed and incorporated into work product need not be returned or destroyed upon withdrawal.
The redline reduces the settlement advance notice period from 45 calendar days to no more than 10 business days.
The redline replaces the requirement to disclose “all material terms of the proposed settlement” with language limiting disclosure to the existence and general nature of the settlement.
The redline extends the surviving confidentiality obligation from 3 years to at least 7 years or makes it indefinite.
The redline adds an express conflicts-waiver carve-out preserving each party’s right to assert claims against other JDA members in future litigation.
The conflicts-waiver carve-out specifically mentions or clearly encompasses contribution and indemnity actions among the preserved future claims.
The redline changes the governing law from New York to Illinois.
The redline adds a provision addressing inadvertent disclosure or clawback of shared materials.
The added clawback provision references Federal Rule of Evidence 502(d) or provides a substantively equivalent contractual clawback mechanism.

The redline adds a provision permitting a party to withhold or restrict sharing materials that are also responsive to a separate government investigation in which other JDA members are not similarly situated.
The redline adds an express right for each party to object to or decline specific information-sharing requests from the Steering Committee.
The added objection right identifies at least one permissible ground: work-product protection, separate-interest privilege, or regulatory sensitivity, or a substantially equivalent concept.
The issues/risk memo classifies the blanket conflicts waiver with no carve-out for future inter-party disputes as “Prohibited” or a “never accept” term under the Vantage JDA Playbook.
The issues/risk memo assigns the blanket conflicts waiver the highest or most severe risk rating used in the memo.
The issues/risk memo classifies the requirement to disclose “all material terms” of a proposed settlement as “Prohibited” or a “never accept” term under the Vantage JDA Playbook.
The issues/risk memo assigns the “all material terms” settlement disclosure requirement the highest or most severe risk rating used in the memo.

The issues/risk memo distinguishes among at least three playbook tiers corresponding to “Required” mandatory changes, “Preferred” recommended changes, and “Prohibited” never-accept terms, using those labels or equivalent classifications.

The issues/risk memo flags the proposed cost-sharing allocation—50% to Kerrigan-Holst and the remaining 50% split equally among the three other parties—as a deviation from the playbook’s preferred pro-rata allocation based on each party’s relative share of plaintiffs’ claimed damages, recalculated quarterly.

The issues/risk memo flags the proposed steering committee composition—one permanent seat for Kerrigan-Holst’s counsel, one rotating seat, and one seat elected by majority vote—as a deviation from the playbook’s preferred equal-representation model, under which each signatory receives one seat or there is no steering committee.

The issues/risk memo flags binding JAMS arbitration in New York, New York, before a single arbitrator as a deviation from the playbook’s preferred approach of mediation before any binding process, followed by litigation in the forum of the underlying case rather than arbitration.

The issues/risk memo flags the obligation to use “commercially reasonable efforts” to make witnesses and documents available for 18 months after settlement as a deviation from the playbook’s preferred position of no affirmative post-settlement cooperation obligation beyond document preservation, and notes that the “commercially reasonable efforts” witness-availability standard is disfavored.
The issues/risk memo assigns a risk rating to each deviation it identifies from the playbook.
The issues/risk memo provides a recommended position or proposed alternative language for each deviation it identifies.
The issues/risk memo identifies Vantage JDA Playbook v4.2, dated September 15, 2024, as the benchmark standard for the review.
The issues/risk memo references the underlying litigation by the case name In re Industrial Fasteners Antitrust Litigation.
The issues/risk memo references the case number 1:23-cv-04871.
The issues/risk memo identifies the court as the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois or N.D. Ill.
The issues/risk memo identifies the absence of a limitation-of-liability clause among the JDA parties for breaches of the agreement as a missing protection.

The redline changes the JDA scope definition’s coverage of “any government investigation concerning the same subject matter” to account for situations where a party may need to withhold materials in a separate government investigation in which other JDA members are not similarly situated.
